{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to treat past interactions as continuing interest in broadly related items, with insufficient attention to the specific purpose of the next choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Direct connections to recently explored artists, franchises, devices, or practical tasks give users clear reasons to choose recommendations.",
    "Complementary products and closely matched musical styles appeal when they extend an established activity or interest."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broad thematic relevance competes with stronger connections to recent interests, specific tasks, and existing equipment.",
    "Recommendations assume specialized projects, compatible equipment, or replacement needs that interaction histories do not establish.",
    "Older seasonal interests and previously purchased product types persist without sufficient evidence of renewed demand."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, theme, terminology, or ecosystem membership appears to substitute for matching the item's actual purpose.",
    "Historical interest appears to imply current demand for similar items, including duplicates and overlapping purchases."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent, specific interests and repeated task-level patterns provide stronger choice signals than broad historical associations.",
    "Exact compatibility, dimensions, quantities, and equipment requirements determine whether practical relevance becomes a plausible purchase.",
    "Useful additions, direct artist connections, and preferred tone or style distinguish compelling next choices from merely related items."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top recommendations too often offer broad relevance without a supported reason to choose the item now, allowing speculative needs, duplicates, and stale interests to crowd out stronger matches.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The share of top-ranked items users would choose for a concrete connection to a recent interest or established task.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to incompatible equipment, unsupported projects, duplication, or excessive specificity.",
    "The frequency with which users prefer a lower-ranked direct match over a higher-ranked broadly related item.",
    "The share of recommendations users cannot assess because available item information does not establish a recognizable connection, tracked separately from explicit mismatches."
  ]
}
